data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel-plus-checklist's reliability gain is genuine only if a control panel using a corrupted or inverted version of the checklist performs strictly worse than the panel using the true checklist on the same evaluation tasks.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The corrupted checklist inadvertently improves structure or forces deeper deliberation, causing the corrupted-checklist panel to outperform both the true-checklist panel and the expert.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The corrupted checklist accidentally retains enough true heuristics to outperform the expert, failing to isolate the semantic contribution of the true rules.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Causal mechanism: By holding the procedural and structural aspects of the checklist constant while corrupting its semantic rule content, we isolate the epistemic contribution of the rules themselves. If the corrupted-checklist panel fails, the original gain is attributable to the correctness of the checklist's rules. If the corrupted-checklist panel still succeeds, the gain was mediated by procedural compliance or wisdom-of-crowds effects, not rule validity.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
